next_step: Run A/B canary with small traffic slice on dedicated pool; deliver eval metrics dashboard by 2025-02-20
notes: Profile: mid-stage B2B search SaaS; customers in legal and financial verticals.
Primary objective: reduce wrong-top-1 retrievals in legal doc search and cut median time-to-first-relevant from 6s -> 2s.
Current stack: in-house SBERT embeddings + Elastic re-rank plugin. Considering migration to Redwood embeddings + cross-encoder reranker for top-N.
Index scale: ~210M passages (split into shards by tenancy), expected growth 2x year-over-year.
Traffic pattern: bursty during workday, peak QPS ~450 reads/sec; p50 target latency for search RPC <= 150ms, p95 <= 600ms.
Cost sensitivity: high — target cost per query (end-to-end) < $0.002 at 70th percentile; willing to pay premium for significant quality wins.
Quality guardrails: strict — legal customers require no degradation vs baseline; asking for formal eval suite + regression alerts.
Quote from CTO: 'We cannot accept even small regressions in top-3; must be data-driven during rollout.'
Security: SSO + SAML required, keys in customer KMS for private deploy, data residency US-only for a set of customers.
Decision drivers: eval pass on recall@10 + reranker precision lift, transparent per-query cost and latency profiling, clear fallback policy when dedicated pool is overloaded.
They asked for a plan for canary + A/B: 5% traffic to Redwood reranker for 2 weeks, evaluate with held-out legal queries and human-in-the-loop checks.
Competition: they are also running PoC with Pinecone + custom cross-encoder; Elastic is baseline for production.
Current contract timeline: procurement starts after exec sign-off post-eval (forecast 2025-03).

workload_requirements: Index size: ~210M short passages (~1.5TB raw embeddings compressed), horizontal sharding required
Embedding model preference: 1536-d dense embeddings (open to 1024/2048) with quantized storage
Reranker approach: bi-encoder for candidate recall + cross-encoder for top-10 re-rank (cost-aware hybrid)
Latency SLO: search + rerank end-to-end p50 <= 150ms, p95 <= 600ms for typical queries
Throughput: sustained 250 QPS, bursting to 450 QPS during peak; autoscale must be predictable
Cache: prefix/KV cache desired for repeat queries; want TTL policies exposed
Cost target: end-to-end query cost < $0.002 at typical mix; willing to accept higher for tail but expect transparent breakdown
Fallbacks: automatic fallback to lightweight reranker or cached results when cross-encoder capacity exhausted
Data policy: CR-sensitive fields should be redacted before indexing; logs retained 180 days
evaluation_plan: Hold-out eval set: 5k legal queries + 2k synthetic edge cases (provided by QQL) — baseline metrics already computed
Metrics: recall@10, mrr@10, top-3 precision, latency distribution, per-query cost, human error-rate on sensitive docs
Regression criteria: any >1.5% absolute drop in top-3 precision flagged as blocker for rollout
A/B design: 5/5/90 split (5% canary Redwood reranker, 5% Pinecone proof, 90% baseline) for 14 days
Canary monitoring: daily automated eval and manual review queue for ambiguous failures; build automatic rollback triggers
Evals integration: Redwood Optimize suggested — run nightly evals and alert on drift; QQL wants dashboard access
Sign-off: Product + Legal must approve both eval pass and ASV (availability & security validation) before procurement
